UnaryOp.doc: Prefix operators admitted by the expression parser: arithmetic negation and logical negation. Wider SQLite set (BitNot ~, unary +) is deferred.

LikeKind.doc: Pattern-match operator family. `Like` is SQL LIKE (case-insensitive, %/_ wildcards). `Glob` is SQL GLOB (case-sensitive, *,?,[abc] wildcards). The two share an AST representation (`Expr::Like`) but the runtime opcode differs — see expr-compile.

BinaryOp.doc: Infix operators admitted by the expression parser, at full SQLite precedence tiers (see master.md §Precedence). IS and the compound comparison operators like BETWEEN/IN/LIKE are deferred.

Eq.doc: `=` or `==` — equality. Both spellings fold to Eq; the parser does not preserve the surface spelling.

NotEq.doc: `!=` or `<>` — inequality. Both fold to NotEq.

Concat.doc: `||` — string concatenation, HIGHEST binary precedence per SQLite.

Expr.doc: Expression AST node. Recursive via Binary/Unary/Call — a target-mapping note covers how each target renders self-referencing variant fields (Rust: Box; C: pointer; Go: pointer; Python/Zig: see mapping). Owned text payloads (string, not str) because the AST outlives the source buffer in typical parser use.

IntLit.doc: Integer literal. Text preserves the original spelling (decimal or hex 0x...).

RealLit.doc: Real literal. Text preserves the original spelling (may include `.` or exponent).

StrLit.doc: String literal. Text is the source lexeme INCLUDING surrounding single quotes; escaped `''` pairs NOT yet unescaped (defer to a later semantic pass).

Col.doc: Column reference. `table` is the optional table qualifier (present iff the source spelled `t.col`); `name` is the column name. Unqualified `col` parses with `table` absent; qualified `t.col` parses with `table = Some(t)`. The qualifier is preserved in the AST; downstream resolution semantics live in each statement's compiler.

Call.doc: Function call: `NAME(arg0, arg1, ...)`. The `*` wildcard argument (e.g. `count(*)`) is deferred; `NAME()` with no args is allowed.

WindowCall.doc: Windowed function call: `NAME(args) OVER ( [PARTITION BY ...] [ORDER BY ...] )`. Admitted in v2 narrow form — no frame clause, no named-window reference. partition_by and order_by may both be empty (then OVER () means single window over all rows). For aggregate-named functions (count/sum/avg/min/max), the compiler maps the inner Call shape to the existing AggFuncKind. Rank-style names (row_number / rank / dense_rank) are treated as zero-arg window kinds. SAME structural relationship to recursion as `Call` — the args list and partition_by list and order_by list each carry sub-Exprs subject to per-target self-recursion mapping.

Unary.doc: Unary (prefix) operator applied to a sub-expression.

Binary.doc: Binary (infix) operator applied to two sub-expressions. `lhs op rhs` — left-associative by the precedence table in master.md.

IsNull.doc: Postfix null-test: `arg IS NULL` (negated=false) or `arg IS NOT NULL` (negated=true). Lower precedence than comparison; higher than AND/OR. The general `IS` operator and `IS DISTINCT FROM` are deferred.

Case.doc: CASE expression (searched form). branches is a non-empty list of (when_expr, then_expr) pairs evaluated in order: the first when_expr that evaluates truthy yields its then_expr. If none match, else_ is evaluated (if present) or Null is returned. Simple-form CASE (`CASE x WHEN v1 THEN r1 ...`) is desugared at parse time: each branch's when_expr becomes `Binary(Eq, clone(x), v_i)`, so downstream compilers only ever see searched form. Precedence: prefix (consumed by parse_prefix), terminated by KwEnd.

Cast.doc: `CAST(expr AS type)` — coerce expr to a named type. type_name is the surface text of the type (uppercase by parser convention: 'INTEGER', 'REAL', 'TEXT', 'BLOB', 'NUMERIC', etc.). The compiler maps type_name to a CastKind; unrecognised type_name → CompileError(deferred). Parsed as a prefix construct (KwCast).

Like.doc: `expr [NOT] LIKE pattern [ESCAPE esc]` and `expr [NOT] GLOB pattern`. kind discriminates LIKE vs GLOB — they share the AST shape but compile to distinct opcodes. negated reflects a leading NOT. escape is present iff source had `ESCAPE <expr>` (LIKE only; parser rejects `GLOB ... ESCAPE ...`). Parsed as a postfix at comparison-tier precedence.

Collate.doc: `expr COLLATE name` — collation annotation. The compiler is a stub for now (returns CompileError 'deferred: COLLATE comparison'); the AST node is preserved so a later semantic pass can wire it to the runtime collation path. name is the surface ident (e.g. 'BINARY', 'NOCASE', 'RTRIM'). Parsed as a postfix at the highest precedence (binds tighter than Concat).

Subquery.doc: α15: scalar subquery `(SELECT ...)` embedded in an expression position. Semantics: run the inner SELECT; if it emits zero rows the expression value is NULL; if it emits one-or-more rows the value is the FIRST row's FIRST column (SQLite semantics — no error on multi-row). Correlated subqueries (inner SELECT references outer columns) are compile-time deferred. Compiler currently clean-stops with 'deferred: scalar subquery'.

Exists.doc: α15: `EXISTS (SELECT ...)`. Value is 1 if the inner SELECT emits at least one row, else 0. `negated=true` flips. `NOT EXISTS` is parsed as `Unary(Not, Exists{negated:false})` rather than `Exists{negated:true}` — the parser leaves negation handling to the existing Unary Not path. Compiler currently clean-stops with 'deferred: EXISTS subquery'.

InSubquery.doc: α15: `expr IN (SELECT ...)` / `expr NOT IN (SELECT ...)`. Compiles by materializing the inner SELECT into a buffer then linear-scanning per outer row. Compiler currently clean-stops with 'deferred: IN subquery'.

CaseBranch.doc: One WHEN/THEN pair inside a Case expression. when_expr is a predicate (already desugared from a simple-form equality if the source used `CASE x WHEN v THEN r`). then_expr is the value to return if when_expr is truthy.

WindowOrderItem.doc: One ORDER BY item inside an OVER clause. Mirrors the OrderByItem shape used by SelectStmt but lives in the expr part to avoid an inverse import. desc=true iff the surface used `DESC`; ASC is the default.

ParseError.doc: Parse error carrying the offending token's position (or the synthetic Eof's position if the error is unexpected-end-of-input) plus an owned message.

ParseOk.doc: Successful parse: the produced expression plus the index of the NEXT token to consume (for composing parse_expr inside larger parsers). `next` will equal `tokens.len() - 1` (the Eof index) when the whole token stream was one expression.

parse_expr.doc: Parse a single SQL expression starting at `start` in the token list `tokens`. Implements a Pratt / operator-precedence algorithm per master.md §Precedence. Tokens MUST terminate with exactly one `Eof` (the tokenizer's contract). Returns ParseOk on success or ParseError on the first failure.
